The only change touching ledger entry types is the v6.0.0 bundle itself ('new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD' + 'mandate create/approve endpoints'); no separate shared-ledger/schema/config change appears in the window, so an independent earlier schema change that would reject MANDATE_HOLD is absent from the change record.

Timing against Task a's onset: v6.0.0 deployed 14:46:00Z, elevated error buckets first appear at 14:56Z (~10 min later), ledger-db disk is already at 94.88% at 14:00Z (pre-deployment) and completes its ramp to 100% at 15:04Z — i.e. disk exhaustion is pre-existing and the DB write errors ('No space left on device' from 15:00:26Z) are resource, not schema, in nature.

Historical precedent for this exact symptom set ('No space left on device' + write failures) is HIST-114 (2025-04-18, ledger-db): root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled' (resource_exhaustion), resolved by dropping the slot — a known disk-fill failure mode, not a new-entry-type rejection.

No historical incident in the searched set combines a 'new ledger entry type' with write failures; the near-symptom ledger-db precedents are HIST-111 (new report query full-table scans, bad_deployment) and HIST-110 (IOPS throttling), and payment-failure precedent HIST-105/HIST-103 were external exchange/bank partner outages — so precedent does not support a schema-rejection root cause.

Rollback of v6.0.0 at 15:12:00Z historically-aligns with rollback resolving bad-deployment incidents (e.g. HIST-111 'added index; query review gate'), but no past incident confirms rollback resolving a disk-full ledger failure — HIST-114's resolution was operational (dropped replication slot), and Task a reported error rate still flat ~60% at 16:56Z after the 15:12Z rollback.
